metadata.case_name: CHUM HOK CHING AND ANOTHER v. CHUNG LAI CHING

injuries.description: Knee contusion with abrasion over the front of both knees (clinical diagnosis knee contusion) following the 26 March 2010 accident
source: the 1st plaintiff was examined by Dr Yip Sai Hang on 26 March 2010 at 23:16 hours, and he was found to have abrasion over the front of both knees, but x-ray showed no fracture. The clinical diagnosis was knee contusion.

injuries.description: Pre-existing right knee injuries (MRI findings dated 27 October 2009: soft tissue edema, large suprapatellar effusion, bone bruises in posterior medial and lateral tibial plateaus, tear in posterior horn of medial meniscus and intrasubstance tear lateral meniscus, ACL tear, partial tears medial and lateral collateral ligaments)
source: In the MRI scan report of the 1st plaintiffs right knee by Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital dated 27 October 2009, the 1st plaintiff was found to have (1) soft tissue edema as well as large suprapatellar effusion, (2) bone bruises in the posterior medial and lateral tibial plateaus, (3) tear in the posterior horn of medial meniscus and intrasubstance tear lateral meniscus, (4) ACL tear, and (5) partial tears medial and lateral collateral ligaments.
injuries.icd_description: Injury to multiple structures of knee

injuries.description: 3mm fresh tear in the tympanic membrane of the left ear with minimal decrease in air conduction (as recorded by Dr Au Wing Wah)
source: physical examination revealed no external injury around both ears, otological examination demonstrated a 3mm fresh tear in the tympanic membrane of the 1st plaintiffs left ear, and tuning fork hearing tests revealed minimal decrease in air conduction in his left ear.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of middle or inner ear

injuries.description: Mild traumatic brain injury / post-concussion syndrome with persistent headache, dizziness, impaired concentration and memory, mood/personality changes and related symptoms
source: On 7 May 2012, the 2nd plaintiff consulted a specialist in neurosurgery, Dr Fung Ching Fai, and she was diagnosed with post-concussion syndrome.

Dr Choa opines that the 2nd plaintiff sustained mild traumatic brain injury. Brain injury did occur because she lost consciousness and had a post-traumatic amnesia of some hours but less than one day.

Dr Yu opines that the 2nd plaintiff has post-concussion syndrome as evidenced by the symptoms of headache, dizziness, impaired concentration, subjective impairment of cognition and memory, irritability and interrupted sleep.
injuries.icd_description: Concussion with loss of consciousness, short duration of less than 30 minutes

injuries.description: Bald spot at the left posterior scalp measured 20 X 15mm, smooth flat and void of hair (scalp scar)
source: both experts confirm that the 2nd plaintiff had (1) a bald spot measured at 20 X 15mm, smooth flat and void of hair at the left posterior scalp;
injuries.icd_description: Other specified superficial injury of scalp

injuries.description: Several abrasion scars over the dorsum and proximal wrist of the left hand and scars on right hand dorsum and knuckle area (various small scars as described by plastic surgeons)
source: several abrasion scars over the dorsum and proximal wrist of the left hand, namely, a linear irregular scar at the radial surface of the proximal wrist measured 20 X 3mm, but it was soft, smooth and barely visible, and two round spots over the mid and ring fingers of the knuckle area measured 10 X 10mm and 7 X 7mm respectively which is slightly raised and firm; and (3) at the right hand dorsum, a round scar measured 8 X 10mm over the wrist, which was soft, smooth and slightly visible, and a round scar over the knuckle area of the ring finger measured 10mm in diameter, which was soft and smooth.
injuries.icd_description: Multiple superficial injuries of wrist or hand

injuries.description: Loss of the fingernail of the left middle finger
source: Loss of the fingernail of the left middle finger.

injuries.description: Soft tissue injury of the neck (whiplash/neck discomfort) with pain and limited rotation on occasion
source: In the medical report dated 3 November 2012 by Dr Brian Choa, ... 5. Neck discomfort: Since the accident, she has become more prone to a cricked neck. When this happens there is pain and limitation of rotation of her head to the right.
Dr Yu opines ... in the accident, there was also mild injury of the neck and low back. This would give rise to soft tissue injury resulting in pain
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain with musculoskeletal signs

injuries.description: Soft tissue injury of the low back with intermittent low back discomfort
source: Dr Choa: 6. Low Back discomfort: This is noticed only from time to time when she twists her back, such as in bending down to retrieve an object from the floor.
Dr Yu opines ... in the accident, there was also mild injury of the neck and low back.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of muscle, fascia or tendon of lower back

manifestations.description: Pain over the left and right knees; pain aggravated by squatting for 5 to 10 minutes; needs to shift weight frequently when squatting
Walking/postures in which he experiences pain; needs to sit down or stretch leg to relieve pain
Headache (throbbing, worse with exertion, disturbs sleep)
Dizziness (momentary bouts causing brief loss of balance)
Impaired concentration and memory; less confident in memory; loses train of thought
Mood/personality changes: more easily irritated, depressed at times, nervous in traffic
Scalp area void of hair at left posterior scalp (bald spot) with associated local pain when touched and pain turning to left side when sleeping
Multiple small scars on hands and wrists; some slightly raised and firm; hands and wrists freely mobile
Neck pain and limited rotation on occasion
Intermittent low back pain aggravated by standing 5 to 10 minutes

treatments_received.treatment: Accident & Emergency treatment at Queen Elizabeth Hospital (examination by Dr Yip Sai Hang for 1st plaintiff on 26 March 2010; and by Dr Lui Yee Chiu Victor for 2nd plaintiff on 26 March 2010)
source: the 1st plaintiff was admitted to the Department of Accident & Emergency of QEH immediately after the accident.

Immediately after the accident on 26 March 2010, the 2nd plaintiff was admitted to the Department of Accident & Emergency of QEH. She was attended by Dr Lui Yee Chiu Victor at 23:55 hours on the same day.

treatments_received.treatment: General Out-patient consultations at Anne Black Health Centre General Out-patient Clinic (ABHCGOPC)
source: On 29 March 2010, the 1st plaintiff attended ABHCGOPC.
The 2nd plaintiff attended ABHCGOPC on 29 March 2010, 1 April 2010 and 7 April 2010 for dressing of the wound on her head.

treatments_received.treatment: Consultation with Dr Au Wing Wah (1st plaintiff) - otological examination and prescription Eurozyme 90mg t.i.d. and Vitamin C 100 mg t.i.d. for 5 days
source: According to Dr Aus medical report dated 7 May 2011, physical examination revealed no external injury around both ears, otological examination demonstrated a 3mm fresh tear in the tympanic membrane of the 1st plaintiffs left ear, and tuning fork hearing tests revealed minimal decrease in air conduction in his left ear. The 1st plaintiff was prescribed with Eurozyme 90mg t.i.d. and Vitamin C 100 mg t.i.d. for 5 days, but he did not return to Dr Au for follow up.

treatments_received.treatment: Operation to mend tear in the ligament of the right knee (January 2010) (1st plaintiff, prior accident)
source: Under cross-examination, the 1st plaintiff admits that he had an operation to mend the tear in the ligament of his right knee in January 2010

treatments_received.treatment: Multiple specialist consultations and follow-ups for 2nd plaintiff including Dr Clifford Loo, Dr Chau Yat Sang, Dr Or Chi Kong, Dr Fung Ching Fai, Dr Brian Choa; neurosurgery follow-ups at QEH and radiology imaging (CT, MRI) and occupational therapy assessments (Rivermead PCS, MOCA)
source: The 2nd plaintiff consulted Dr Clifford Loo ... multiple follow ups.
On 7 May 2012, the 2nd plaintiff consulted a specialist in neurosurgery, Dr Fung Ching Fai, and she was diagnosed with post-concussion syndrome.

The 2nd plaintiff was examined by the Department of Radiology & Imaging of QEH on 3 July 2012. According to its report dated 9 July 2012, the clinical diagnosis was post-concussion syndrome but no abnormality was noted.

the Rivermead Post Concussion Symptoms (PCS) Questionnaire dated 30 May 2012, it shows that the score of the 2nd plaintiff was 61 out of 64. Also, in the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MOCA) Hong Kong Version dated 30 May 2012, the 2nd plaintiff scored 26 out of 30.
In relation to the scar over her left head, the 2nd plaintiff states that she received 10 stitches

treatments_future.treatment: Plastic surgery (excision revision) for scars (surgeon's fee $10,000 and follow-up charges $3,000) (2nd plaintiff)
source: Both Dr Au and Dr Ian Nicolson ... the scars on her hands can be improved by plastic surgery in the form of excision revision, the costs of which are (1) surgeon's fee in the amount of $10,000.00 and (2) followed up charges in the amount of $3,000.00.
treatments_future.vmis_procedure: Local excision or destruction of lesion or tissue of skin and subcutaneous tissue

treatments_future.treatment: Use of a tricyclic drug (e.g. Amitriptyline) supervised by a neurologist/psychiatrist, estimated cost $15,000 over about six months (2nd plaintiff)
source: Dr Choa opines ... she is a good candidate for the use of medication such as a tricyclic drug like amitriptyline ... would cost an estimated $15,000.00 over about a six-month period.
Dr Yu agrees ... The expenses for such treatment by a neurologist or a psychiatrist would be about $15,000.00 over a 6 month period.

losses.description: Pain, reduced function and ongoing discomfort in the knees (pain aggravated by squatting, needs to shift weight frequently), arising from the knee contusion and aggravated by pre-existing right knee injury
Aggravated right knee condition due to combination of pre-existing right knee injuries and the present accident (pre-existing ACL/meniscal/collateral ligament injuries)
Bald spot (20 X 15mm) at left posterior scalp and multiple scars on dorsum and proximal wrist of left hand and scars on right hand
Impaired concentration and memory; less confident in memory; difficulty organizing thoughts affecting work
Increased irritability and periods of low mood since the accident; nervousness in traffic

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Apprehension about traffic and inability to resume motorcycle rides; nervous in traffic

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Prior pastimes included hiking, running and driving motorcycles; after the accident the 2nd plaintiff resumed swimming but not hiking or running and stopped motorcycle rides
Reduced working ability, slower typing, memory issues and concerns about possibly being dismissed from long-term employment; awarded loss of earning capacity
